subject.title: GitHub OAuth consent screen uses personal ClawdHub app branding

question: Should production GitHub sign-in now move to an official OpenClaw/ClawHub-owned OAuth App, and who will rotate and validate the Convex production OAuth credentials?
rationale: The source tree can show which credentials select the GitHub provider, but only maintainers/operators can create or transfer the OAuth App, rotate production secrets, and accept the auth-availability risk during rollout.

options.title: Move to an official app now
options.body: Create or transfer the OAuth App to official ownership, rotate production AUTH_GITHUB_ID/AUTH_GITHUB_SECRET, and verify fresh browser plus CLI auth before closing.

options.title: Temporarily keep the personal app
options.body: Document the accepted ownership risk and leave this issue open until an official app migration window is scheduled.

options.title: Close only after live proof
options.body: If operators already migrated the app, attach fresh consent-screen and CLI auth proof showing official branding before closing.

recommendation.title: Move to an official app now
recommendation.body: Create or transfer the OAuth App to official ownership, rotate production AUTH_GITHUB_ID/AUTH_GITHUB_SECRET, and verify fresh browser plus CLI auth before closing.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS and current blame route the auth/security and deploy surfaces to Patrick-Erichsen, making this the best available decision owner signal.
